text:
lina: customer reports 401 invalid_api_key when streaming chat but embeddings endpoint works for same key.

devon: any request logs / full headers (redact key)?

lina: here's the curl they used:
```bash
curl -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
embeddings call with same key returned 200 earlier.

ashwin: Hmm. Is this a customer generated via SSO? any note about 'org-scoped' keys?

lina: Yes — they said key was provisioned by their SSO admin and labeled 'org-sso'.

ashwin: That explains it — org-scoped keys are metadata-only and must be exchanged via our SSO token-exchange endpoint for per-session tokens. Direct use will 401 for endpoints that require customer-scoped tokens (streaming/chat). Embeddings allow org-key because it's an audit-only flow.

devon: Can you share the error body? The API should give hint 'key requires exchange' if that's the case.

lina: error body: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"key invalid for this route"}`. No exchange hint.

support-bot: :eyes: routed to auth-team for quick followup.

ashwin: Action: ask customer to try token-exchange flow:
```bash
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/exchange \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer ORG_KEY' \
 -d '{"scope":"chat:session"}'
```
use returned token for stream request. Also I'll add a clearer error message on API side.

lina: ok passing steps to customer, will report back. Thanks.
